final_answer: Antibiotic resistance occurs when bacteria evolve mechanisms to survive exposure to antibiotics. This is an example of natural selection, where bacteria that possess resistance genes are more likely to survive and reproduce in the presence of antibiotics, passing these genes to subsequent generations. Overprescription of antibiotics accelerates this process by increasing the selective pressure on bacterial populations, leading to a higher frequency of resistant strains. Additionally, the misuse of antibiotics in both human medicine and agriculture contributes to the spread of resistance. Resistance genes can also be transferred between bacteria through horizontal gene transfer, further spreading resistance traits. Therefore, overprescription not only promotes the emergence of resistant strains but also enables their proliferation and dissemination.
